warRiskPremium.note: NEW (checked 2026-10-04): NO FRESH WAR-RISK QUOTE; VALUE HELD. Jev gate failed on source_quality (1.48<1.5). Argus (early Oct): a 2004-built VLCC provisionally hired at $2M PER DAY to transit Hormuz (vs USG-China $366,704/d on Oct 1); UKMTO reported projectiles struck 3 ships in the strait — the 3-10% of hull value band stands. Brent ~$95-102; G7 announced emergency fuel-reserve release (Time, Oct 3). NEW (checked 2026-09-27): RED-SEA WAR-RISK TRIPLED; HORMUZ BAND HOLDING — VALUE UNCHANGED. Reuters (Sep 25, via Insurance Journal/Baird Maritime): quoted war-risk premiums for Saudi-linked tankers calling at Yanbu have risen to ~3% of vessel value (vs <1% in early July); south of Yanbu incl. Jizan can reach 7%, approaching Hormuz levels (6-9% of hull value); Red Sea transits with no Saudi connection pay just 0.2-0.3%. A 7-day Yanbu voyage can cost ~$3M, ~$7M from further south or via Hormuz (vs >=$100K pre-war); average price of old tankers above $100M as producers rush to buy their own tonnage; Saudi appointed Saudi Reinsurance Co to lead its marine war-risk pool. Jev gate: has_new_data 0.92 but source_quality 1.28 (<1.5) -> value held at the 3-10% band. Brent settled $104.32 on Sep 25 (-2.1% d/d, +2% w/w) as US-Iran phased-reopening talks surfaced. NEW (checked 2026-09-20): NO FRESH INSURANCE PRINT; OIL SPIKE FADED. No new war-risk quote broke this week — the band stands at 3-10% of hull value (pre-war 0.25%): a $100M tanker faces $3-10M of premium vs ~$250K before the war. Brent spiked to a multi-month high near $107-109 on Sep 15 then settled $104.61 (Sep 11) and eased to $99.29 by Sep 19 (-5.09% w/w) as the Oman-hosted GCC-Iran shipping talks were postponed. PRIOR (checked 2026-09-13): TRANSIT COSTS RE-ESCALATED TO $10-20M PER SHIP. ENOC director Paul Bradshaw at APPEC (Sep 9, Reuters/Baird Maritime): full war-risk + cargo cost to move crude out of the Gulf has escalated into the $10 MILLION TO $20 MILLION PER SHIP range; cargo insurance now 5-6% of cargo value and up to 10% of cargo for exit cover (vs ~zero pre-war) — 'another $10 million on your cargo insurance'; SOME MARKET PARTICIPANTS ARE NOW TRANSITING WITH NO INSURANCE AT ALL; more national oil companies have taken their own shipping back in-house precisely so they retain the ability to exit during conflict; the pool of shipowners willing to take the risk is shrinking. Hull war-risk remains quoted in the 3-10% of hull value band (pre-war 0.25%) — a $100M tanker faces $3-10M of premium vs ~$250K before the war (The National/Marsh). Structural repricing permanent. Backdrop: Brent settled $101.21 on Sep 9 (first triple-digit close since July), $104.61 on Sep 11 — +9% w/w, +17.6% m/m, +56% YoY — after the Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown and Houthi advances on Bab el-Mandeb; IEA cut its 2026 global oil demand forecast by 2.5 mb/d (largest annual contraction since Covid). PRECEDING CONTEXT: Sept 1 'tanker-for-tanker' US strikes on Iranian government tankers halted the late-Aug premium easing (3-8%); claims from the conflict exceed $2B across 70+ cases — second-largest marine-insurer hit in a decade after the 2024 Baltimore bridge; ~$7-8/bbl of crude cost attributable to war-risk insurance; Lloyd's facing ~£1.4B in losses. High-risk zone extended ~800km north along Saudi Red Sea coast; charterers' liability standard cover has blanket exclusion for Saudi-linked vessels; Saudi seeking a state-backed guarantee scheme. De facto $3-10M toll per tanker persists. Updated 2026-09-27
warRiskPremium.note_zh: 新（核查于2026-10-04）：无新战争险报价；数值保持。Jev闸门source_quality未过（1.48<1.5）。Argus（10月初）：一艘2004年建VLCC以每天200万美元的临时租金经霍尔木兹（vs 美湾-中国10月1日$366,704/天）；UKMTO报告峡内3艘船被投射物击中——船体价值3-10%区间维持。布伦特约$95-102；G7宣布释放应急燃料储备（Time，10月3日）。 新（核查于2026-09-27）：红海战争险涨两倍，霍尔木兹区间维持——数值未变。路透（9月25日，经Insurance Journal/Baird Maritime）：沙特关联船只挂靠延布的战争险报价升至船体价值约3%（7月初<1%）；延布以南含吉赞可达7%、逼近霍尔木兹水平（6-9%）；无沙特关联的红海通行仅0.2-0.3%。7天期延布航程保费可约300万美元，更南或经霍尔木兹约700万美元（战前≥10万）；旧油轮均价破1亿美元（产油国抢购自有船队）；沙特指定沙特再保险公司牵头其海运战争险池。Jev闸门：has_new_data 0.92但source_quality 1.28（<1.5）→数值保持3-10%区间。布伦特9月25日结算$104.32（日跌2.1%、周涨2%），因美伊分阶段重开谈判浮现。 新（核查于2026-09-20）：本周无新保费报价，油价冲高后回落。战争险仍报船体价值3-10%区间（战前0.25%）——1亿美元油轮保费300万-1000万美元 vs 战前约25万美元。布伦特9月15日冲至约$107-109的数月高点，9月11日结算$104.61，因阿曼主办的 GCC-伊朗航运谈判延期，9月19日回落至$99.29（周跌5.09%）。前情（核查于2026-09-13）：全程通行成本重新升至每船$1000-2000万。ENOC董事Paul Bradshaw在APPEC（9月9日，路透/Baird Maritime）：把原油运出海湾的战争险+货物险总成本已升至每船1000万至2000万美元区间；货物险现为货值5-6%，出港保险可达货值10%（战前近零）——'你的货物险上又是1000万美元'；部分市场参与者现已完全无保险通行；更多国家石油公司把航运收回自营，正是为了在冲突时保留撤出能力；愿意承担风险的船东池在收缩。船体战争险仍在船体价值3-10%区间（战前0.25%）——一艘1亿美元油轮面临300万-1000万美元保费，战前约25万美元（The National/Marsh）。结构性重定价已属永久。背景：布伦特9月9日结算$101.21（7月以来首次三位数收盘），9月11日$104.61——周涨9%、月涨17.6%、年涨56%——此前沙特东西管道停运、胡塞向曼德海峡推进；IEA将2026年全球石油需求预测下调250万桶/天（疫情以来最大年度收缩）。前情：9月1日美方'以船换船'打击伊朗政府油轮，中止了8月底的保费回落（3-8%）；冲突理赔超$20亿、涉70+案例，为十年来仅次于2024年巴尔的摩大桥事件的第二大海事保险打击；每桶原油成本中约$7-8归因于战争险；劳合社面临约£14亿损失。高风险区域沿沙特红海海岸向北延伸约800公里；承租人标准责任险对沙特关联船只设全盘排除条款；沙特寻求国家担保机制。每艘油轮实际负担300-1000万美元过路成本。更新于 2026-09-27

straitThroughput.note: NEW (checked 2026-10-11): TRANSITS AT TWO-MONTH LOW — VALUE UPDATED (Jev gate PASSED: has_new_data 0.91, source_quality 1.53). Kpler via Maritime Executive (Oct 8): 7 commodity vessels transited Oct 6 — lowest since Jul 23; LSEG counted 8 (incl. 5 tankers) vs 14 on Monday Oct 5 and an average >20/day earlier in the month. Kpler note (Oct 6): crude crossing the strait fell 27% from the wartime high to at least 10.1M b/d — back to the September average but only 74% of pre-war level. Iran Intl (Oct 7): Kpler recorded 5 commodity vessels Saturday and NONE on Sunday vs 31 the previous weekend; IRGC adviser Naqdi: 'The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and the armed forces have full control over it' until Iran's demands are met. Windward (Oct 9): 16 attacks in 10 days on Gulf shipping; a tanker was struck by projectiles 51nm off Madinat ash Shamal (Oct 7, first attack outside the strait since Sep 9) and another east of Fujairah (Oct 8); UKMTO has logged at least one attack/day since Oct 2. Context from prior check (2026-10-04): crude had returned to pre-war 7-day average of 13.5M b/d (Sep 28) under US escort + pipelines; refined products still 677K b/d vs 3.6M prewar; ~40% of Gulf crude bypasses Hormuz. PRIOR (checked 2026-10-04): CRUDE BACK TO PREWAR VOLUMES — VALUE HELD (Jev source_quality 1.31<1.5). Kpler via CNBC (Sep 30): 7-day average of crude transiting Hormuz hit 13.5M b/d as of Monday Sep 28 — matching the prewar baseline — under the US escort regime plus pipelines; refined products still only 677K b/d vs 3.6M prewar; ~40% of Gulf crude now bypasses Hormuz (vs 17% prewar). Windward counted 17 vessels through Monday Sep 28 (16 the day before), most with transponders off. Commodity-vessel transits remain in the 9-18/day band recorded last cycle. NEW (checked 2026-09-27): TRANSITS OFF THE SEP-16 LOW BUT STILL ~HALF NORMAL — VALUE UNCHANGED. Kpler via Reuters (Sep 25): Hormuz commodity-vessel transits fell to 9 on Thu Sep 24 from 14 the day before, vs a 10-day average of 18; crude flows through Hormuz reached 33.7M barrels this week, roughly on track with the previous week. The National/Kpler (Sep 21): only 14 vessels transited over the weekend of Sep 19-20 vs 36 the prior weekend. US News/Kpler (Sep 20): 22 tankers (mostly VLCCs) carrying 42M barrels exited the strait in the week of Sep 13 (Saudi Arabia and Iraq 43% each). Jev gate: has_new_data 0.91, source_quality 1.42 (<1.5) -> value held; the existing band still captures the 3-14/day range. NEW (checked 2026-09-20): TRANSITS CRASHED TO 3 ON SEP 16. Kpler preliminary data via The Hindu (Sep 17): commodity-vessel transits through Hormuz fell to just 3 on Wednesday Sep 16, down from 12 on Sep 15 and far below the 10-day average of ~17 — an empty Supramax dry bulk ship entered via the Iranian route, an empty product tanker entered via a dark route, and a Panamax tanker exited via a dark route (all AIS-visible; dark transits excluded). UANI/JMIC (Sep 14): 70 US-facilitated transits over the 72 hours Sep 10-12, 1,600 cumulative since Jun 20; ~23/day average since the July ~4.5/day trough — still ~83% below the pre-war ~138/day. Lloyd's List Intelligence (Sep 9): at least 112 non-Iranian-linked crude-tanker transits in August vs 72 in July; 191 westbound transits in August vs 160 in July; August weekly average 78 transits vs 48 before the temporary MoU recovery; preliminary 82 non-Iranian-linked transits Aug 24-30 vs 100 the week before. PRIOR (checked 2026-09-13): TRANSITS STILL SINGLE-DIGIT, DATA WAR INTACT. Reuters (Sep 10): vessel transits via Hormuz FELL to 7 on Wednesday Sep 9 from 12 the previous day — also below the 10-day average of 14. UANI/JMIC (Sep 11): 901 vessels have transited since June 18, 1,514 since the war began (pre-war baseline ~138/day); since the July low of ~4.5 transits/day the rate has recovered to an average of ~23/day — i.e. still ~83% below normal. USNI News (Sep 4): US-facilitated transits varied wildly — 65 over Aug 27-29 vs 37 over Aug 25-26; JMIC figures still do NOT match the Trump administration's 30-40 ships/day claim. Dark transits + ship-to-ship transfers are the workaround; ADNOC continues mainly-dark shuttle runs; many transiting ships are state-subsidised by Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and Kuwait, whose sovereign backing lets them absorb the risk. Flows: dated Brent (the benchmark pricing ~two-thirds of supply) has been above $100 since Sep 3 (LSEG); Brent settled $101.21 Sep 9 (first triple-digit close since July) and $104.61 Sep 11 (+9% w/w). UKMTO continues to log incidents; JWC listing unchanged. PRECEDING CONTEXT: Kpler showed 4-6 commodity vessels/day Sep 1-3 vs ~14 late-Aug avg; PortWatch 6 transits vs ~85/day pre-crisis; ~450 vessels waiting. War-risk costs make many transits uneconomic. Updated 2026-09-27

irgcStatementFreq.note: NEW (checked 2026-10-11): still crisis-level; value held (Jev has_new_data 0.76 but source_quality 1.47 < 1.5). IRGC adviser Mohammadreza Naqdi (Oct 7, Iran Intl): 'The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and the armed forces have full control over it' until Iran's demands are met; at least 7 tanker attacks reported in the first week of October; 16 attacks in 10 days per Windward. Diplomatic track: Iran-Oman agreed on safe-transit-route coordinates (FM spokesman Baghaei, Oct 8, IRNA/Mehr) to be lodged with the relevant international body; Iran's response to US proposals to come via mediators. UKMTO logging an attack a day since Oct 2. NEW (checked 2026-10-04): STILL CRISIS-LEVEL; VALUE HELD (Jev has_new_data 0.24). UKMTO (Oct 1 report): unknown projectiles struck three ships in the strait; Soufan Center: IRGC might have fired on three tankers. IRGC (Fri Oct 2): ready to deliver an 'immediate, painful, regret-inducing response' to any US/Israel aggression. Iran received a formal US response to its 7-day reopening plan (Sep 30 cabinet); Supreme Leader statement (Sep 28) claimed US warships pulled back from Chabahar-area blockade positions. NEW (checked 2026-09-27): STILL CRISIS-LEVEL. Iran's air-defence forces shot down an advanced 'orbital vehicle' drone over the Strait of Hormuz on Sep 20 (unidentified operator, CCTV/Edgen). Iran's FM proposed reopening Hormuz within 7 days if Washington lifts its naval blockade, unfreezes assets and ends the war 'on all fronts'; an Iranian security official set out that sequence on Sep 19. Statement tempo remains far above the 5/week warning line. NEW (checked 2026-09-20): STILL CRISIS-LEVEL — NOW ENFORCED VESSEL BY VESSEL. Sep 14 (Xinhua/Sepah News): IRGC Navy said the supertanker EL GAIA exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines on the 'forbidden' southern route; the IRGC declared the strait 'closed'; Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) warned insurers, P&I clubs and classification societies against servicing listed 'violating' vessels. Sep 16 (Mehr News, IRGC PR): IRGC Aerospace Force downed the US military's 52nd MQ-9 drone over Qeshm Island. Sep 18 (Tasnim, IRGC Navy Cdr Rear Adm. Ali Ozmaei): the Togo-flagged tanker 'Trend' was hit and set on fire for an 'illegal' transit — 'illegal passage through the Strait of Hormuz will have no outcome other than the destruction of the offending vessel'. Sep 16 (Caliber.Az): IRGC Navy political deputy Ali Mohammadi — no vessel can move through the Persian Gulf, Hormuz or Gulf of Oman without being monitored by Iran. Statement tempo therefore stays far above the 5/week 'warning' line. PRIOR (checked 2026-09-13): HEAVIEST EXCHANGE OF THE WAR SINCE SEPT 1. Sep 7: Iran declared it would announce a Hormuz 'prohibited zone' within days. Sep 8: after the IRGC twice fired ballistic missiles at a US Navy warship over two days, CENTCOM DISABLED 5 Iranian tankers — Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1 and Risco in the Sea of Oman plus Darya near Kharg Island (crews evacuated first). Also Sep 8: IRGC announced it had SEIZED a US Navy unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) and published recovery footage; CENTCOM confirmed the drone was American but an older model with no sensitive sensors or classified kit, recovered after a technical malfunction. Sep 9 (dawn statement): IRGC claimed it had struck 2 US destroyers, 8 oil tankers and 10 other vessels in an operation named 'Punishing the Aggressors' — retaliation for the US strikes on Iranian tankers — and said the 10 were trying to transit the 'prohibited and unsafe' Hormuz zone under US escort (claims unconfirmed; no US confirmation of damage). Same statement announced a ballistic-missile salvo on Al Azraq airbase in Jordan targeting US F-35/F-16/F-15s: Jordan's armed forces said 20 missiles were fired, 18 intercepted and destroyed, 2 fell in unpopulated areas, no casualties. fleetPosition.note: NEW (checked 2026-10-04): US REINFORCEMENT — VALUE HELD (Jev 0.53/0.96 below gate). AP (Oct 3): Trump sending another carrier and 10,000 sailors/Marines to the region (~9,000 extra forces per CBS Oct 2); Trump vows war will end 'right after the election' or sooner; Iranian officials see little deal prospect before the Nov 3 midterms and high escalation risk after. Iran inflation ~90%, rial record low. US formal response to Iran's 7-day plan delivered via Doha Sep 29-30; sequencing dispute (who moves first) unresolved. NEW (checked 2026-09-27): REOPENING NOW TIED TO THE US BLOCKADE. Iran made Hormuz reopening conditional on the US lifting its naval blockade of Iranian ports and returning to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding; Qatari/Pakistani mediators told Tehran Washington is ready to negotiate, while the White House said Trump is open to talks but the US is under no pressure. NSA Bahrain remains unusable; WSJ/Navy Times report damage possibly ~$400M. NEW (checked 2026-09-20): US-IRAN FIRE PAUSE ENTERS A TENTH DAY. GlobalSecurity.org Day-204 update (Sep 19): 'the fire pause entered a tenth day with no new Iranian attack on any host state reported' through the 0500 ET cutoff, and no new US strike wave against Iran since the ~100-target 1 September package. The pause is narrow, not a settlement: the IRGC keeps enforcing the Hormuz closure against individual tankers (EL GAIA mines, Trend hit) while the US keeps the 'tanker-for-tanker' posture, and the 5th Fleet Bahrain hub remains unusable. PRIOR (checked 2026-09-13): THE US NAVY HAS EFFECTIVELY LOST ITS BAHRAIN HUB. Acting Navy Secretary Cao (Sep 11) acknowledged Iranian attacks early in the war left the 5th Fleet headquarters at Naval Support Activity Bahrain damaged and UNABLE TO SUPPORT USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN OPERATIONS — the carrier crew had 'no place for them to pull in'; the Navy's top uniformed officer Adm. Daryl Caudle said the service would not return to NSA Bahrain 'anytime soon'. Iran publicly welcomed the admission (AA, Sep 11); open-source/satellite imagery had already indicated substantial damage. This is the biggest basing setback of the war and licenses sustained IRGC messaging about US force-posture vulnerability. Exchange tempo: the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US warship twice over Sep 7-8 (US: evaded, no damage); CENTCOM then disabled 5 Iranian tankers (Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, Risco, Darya) — the 'tanker-for-tanker' policy in action, with Rubio promising more; the IRGC claimed 2 US destroyers and 18 vessels hit on Sep 9 and fired 20 ballistic missiles at Al Azraq, Jordan (18 intercepted). US-facilitated transits varied 37-65/day over Aug 25-29 (USNI) — far above independent tracker counts. CENTCOM (Adm. Cooper) still says lanes are 'open, momentum building'; independent trackers count 7-14/day. Iranian crude exports remain halted; ~86-87 Iranian-linked vessels rerouted since July; Treasury SDN'd Golden Global Bank (Sep 4) over conversion of Iranian oil proceeds into cash/gold. PRECEDING: first 'tanker-for-tanker' strikes on Iranian tankers Sep 1 + ~100-target package. Updated 2026-09-27

saudiUaeStance.note: NEW (checked 2026-10-04): EAST-WEST PIPELINE RESTARTING — VALUE HELD (Jev 0.11 below gate). Barchart headline (Sep 29-30): 'Brent Trims Gains as Key Saudi Pipeline Restarts' — the East-West pipeline shut on Sep 10 is coming back; CNBC (Sep 30): Riyadh had shifted exports back through Hormuz under the US-protected shuttle during the outage. CBS (Oct 2): Saudi coalition accuses Houthis of drone attack on Medina. G7 emergency fuel-reserve release announced (Oct). NEW (checked 2026-09-27): HOUTHIS HIT SAUDI CITIES; YANBU STILL SHUT. Iran-aligned Houthis launched missiles toward Saudi cities including Yanbu and Taif on Sep 24; loadings at Yanbu have not resumed since the East-West pipeline shutdown. Saudi appointed the Saudi Reinsurance Company to lead its marine war-risk pool and denied Iraq's allegation it bought 25 tankers (~$4.5B). GCC secretary-general Jassim al-Budaiwi: Hormuz must not be turned into 'a bargaining chip'. NEW (checked 2026-09-20): GULF DIPLOMACY STALLED; SAUDI STRETCHED FURTHER. The Oman-hosted GCC-Iran meeting on Hormuz scheduled for Mon Sep 14 was POSTPONED 'in the interests of consensus' (Omani FM Badr Albusaidi, Sep 13); an Iranian FM official said it was deferred at the request of some regional states via a joint Tehran-Muscat decision, Iranian state media suggested Washington interfered while Saudi Arabia sought to add an untenable term to a draft, and only Iraq had publicly confirmed attendance. Saudi Arabia and Egypt's leaders called for free navigation in the Red Sea after Riyadh vowed a firm response to Houthi attacks; Saudi briefly issued and lifted emergency alerts for Yanbu, Jeddah, Taif, Abha and Jazan; Saudi told European customers some late-September crude cargoes will be cancelled (Reuters, three sources); MBS met Egypt's Sisi in Cairo (Tue Sep 15) to discuss the crisis; a Saudi-led coalition said Houthi missile/drone attacks wounded 13 civilians and the UN Security Council was due to meet on the Houthi offensive. The Houthis completed their conquest of Yemen's western coastline and Perim Island, positioning them to enforce their declared blockade on Saudi-linked shipping via Bab el-Mandeb. PRIOR (checked 2026-09-13): ALLIANCE STRAIN BROADENING — SAUDI NOW SQUEEZED ON BOTH SIDES OF THE PENINSULA. Sep 10 (Thu): Saudi Arabia SHUT DOWN its East-West pipeline (745 miles/1,200km, built in the 1980s as the Hormuz bypass) after multiple drone strikes in the Riyadh and Medina regions — both Baghdad and Riyadh said the drones came from Iraq, where Iran-backed militias operate; several people injured; Iraq dismissed a military commander in response. The line had been moving 4-5 mb/d (4-5% of global supply) in recent months, per Kpler/analysts. Saudi said it would NOT retaliate for now at the Iraqi PM's request, reserving the right to act. Same window: Houthis seized the port city of Mokha and the Red Sea island of Perim, giving them control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb gateway; the group says it is imposing an embargo on Saudi oil shipments and diplomats say it is eyeing a toll akin to Iran's. Kpler: Saudi oil exports to Asia fell from ~3.4 mb/d in June to 128K bpd in August, recovering to ~700K bpd this month. MBS called Trump at least twice on Sep 10 to request US military help against the Houthis (Reuters, confirming Axios); Washington declined direct military action for now, offering intelligence-sharing and targeting help only — the White House is 'not enthusiastic about getting involved'. Analysts (ACLED/Ratney): Saudi has fewer interceptors available because of the US-Iran conflict; Houthi weaponry is more sophisticated than a decade ago. UAE (Trade Minister Al Zeyoudi, Hili Forum, Sep 8): Hormuz is a 'red line' — 'no country owns the Strait of Hormuz, and no country should determine who can and can't access it'; Abu Dhabi is accelerating a PERMANENT shift away from Hormuz — east-coast ports Khor Fakkan and Fujairah, new logistics corridors via Oman's Sohar and Duqm, and a new pipeline to export Abu Dhabi crude via the Gulf of Oman; the June pledge to cut Hormuz dependency to 'zero' is no longer classed as a temporary workaround. Oil: Brent above $100 (dated Brent since Sep 3). saudiUaeStance.note_zh: 新（核查于2026-10-04）：东西管道重启中——数值保持（Jev 0.11未过闸）。Barchart标题（9月29-30日）：'沙特关键管道重启，布伦特回吐涨幅'——9月10日停运的东西管道正在恢复；CNBC（9月30日）：停运期间利雅得经美军护航穿梭体系改走霍尔木兹。CBS（10月2日）：沙特联军指胡塞无人机袭击麦地那。G7宣布释放应急燃料储备（10月）。 新（核查于2026-09-27）：胡塞打击沙特城市，延布仍未恢复。9月24日伊朗支持的胡塞向包括延布和塔伊夫在内的沙特城市发射导弹；自东西管道停运以来延布装货尚未恢复。沙特指定沙特再保险公司牵头其海运战争险池，并否认伊拉克关于其购买25艘油轮（约45亿美元）的说法。海合会秘书长布达维：霍尔木兹不得成为'筹码'。 新（核查于2026-09-20）：海湾外交受挫，沙特进一步被拉伸。原定9月14日（周一）在阿曼举行的海合会与伊朗霍尔木兹会谈被'以共识为重'为由推迟（阿曼外长巴德尔·布赛义迪，9月13日）；伊朗外交部官员称系部分地区国家要求、经德黑兰与马斯喀特共同决定推迟，伊朗官媒暗示华盛顿干预、沙特试图在草案中加入不可接受的条款，此前仅伊拉克公开确认出席。沙特与埃及领导人呼吁红海航行自由（利雅得誓言对胡塞袭击作出强硬回应）；沙特一度对延布、吉达、塔伊夫、阿卜哈、吉赞发布后撤销紧急警报；沙特告知欧洲客户部分9月下旬原油货载将被取消（路透，三名消息人士）；MBS 9月15日（周二）在开罗会见埃及总统塞西讨论危机；沙特领导的联军称胡塞导弹/无人机袭击致13名平民受伤，联合国安理会就胡塞攻势开会。胡塞完成对也门西海岸与丕林岛的占领，具备对经曼德海峡的沙特关联航运执行其宣布的封锁的能力。前情（核查于2026-09-13）：同盟张力扩大——沙特在半岛两侧同时受压。9月10日（周四）：沙特在利雅得和麦地那地区遭多起无人机袭击后关闭东西管道（745英里/1200公里，1980年代为绕过霍尔木兹而建）——巴格达与利雅得均称无人机来自伊朗支持的民兵活动的伊拉克；数人受伤；伊拉克随后撤换一名军事指挥官。据Kpler/分析人士，该管道近月日均输送400-500万桶（占全球供应4-5%）。沙特表示应伊拉克总理请求暂不报复，但保留采取行动的权利。同一窗口：胡塞武装夺取港口城市摩卡和红海岛屿丕林岛，从而控制也门红海沿岸与曼德海峡门户；该组织称正对沙特石油出口实施禁运，外交人士称其正考虑征收类似伊朗的通行费。Kpler：沙特对亚洲石油出口从6月约340万桶/天降至8月的12.8万桶/天，本月回升至约70万桶/天。MBS 9月10日至少两次致电特朗普请求美军对胡塞提供军事支援（路透，证实Axios报道）；华盛顿暂拒直接军事行动，仅提供情报共享与目标定位支持——白宫'并不热衷于介入'。分析人士（ACLED/Ratney）：因美伊冲突，沙特可用拦截弹减少；胡塞武器较十年前更为先进。阿联酋（外贸部长Al Zeyoudi，Hili论坛，9月8日）：霍尔木兹是'红线'——'没有哪个国家拥有霍尔木兹海峡，也不应有国家决定谁能进出'；阿布扎比正加速永久性摆脱霍尔木兹——东岸的豪尔费坎和富查伊拉港、经阿曼苏哈尔和杜库姆的新物流走廊、以及经阿曼湾出口阿布扎比原油的新管道；6月提出的将霍尔木兹依赖降至'零'不再被列为临时权宜。油价：布伦特高于$100（即期布伦特自9月3日起）。前瞻信号：海湾合作委员会外长预计9月14日（周一）在阿曼与伊朗外长会面，讨论临时航运管理安排。前情：沙特此前已转经埃及SUMED输送约190万桶/天；胡塞封锁已使红海出口在8月降至6.4万桶/天。更新于 2026-09-27
